subdomain: 2.4 Optimize context windows and manage token usage

en.question: A tool-heavy assistant has a durable client-side audit transcript but sends many obsolete tool results back on each request. The chosen model and platform support the cited beta server-side tool-result clearing strategy. Which expectations should guide its use to recover active context? Select 2 answers.

options.text: Each removed result will be replaced by a semantic summary that retains all its important facts.
options.note: Tool-result clearing replaces removed content with placeholders, not guaranteed semantic summaries. Facts still needed later require deliberate retention or retrieval.

options.text: The client can retain the full unmodified transcript while the server clears eligible content before the model receives it.
options.note: Server-side editing changes model-visible context without requiring the client to overwrite its audit history. Client retention and active-context selection are separate concerns.

options.text: The client must overwrite its stored transcript with the placeholders to keep future requests synchronized.
options.note: The documented strategy does not require synchronization to an edited client copy. Rewriting the audit record would unnecessarily discard the original tool evidence.

options.text: Clearing can invalidate affected cached prefixes, so the team should balance recovered context against fresh cache writes.
options.note: Removing content changes the reusable prefix from the affected position. Recovered capacity can be worthwhile, but cache-processing savings are not preserved automatically.
